name: house-escape/index
title: Visiting Hours: the house tips (Night 2's escape, room by room)
subtitle: The escape rebuilt as the night's peak: eleven rooms the house can't hold, each with its own light and sound, folding shut behind her. One still from each checkpoint, looking ahead. At full speed it takes about a minute (62 to 64 s), with a checkpoint every 10 to 20 s.
questions: Ceilings: closed in (the default, shown here: every room but the observatory has one, so the hallways and kitchens feel shut in), or open to the sky over the walls? It's one switch.

Theo's window: if Lena ends unsure, Theo opens a window beside the stairwell door, and climbing through it skips the drop. If she condemns Nadia, the house folds faster behind her there instead. Do those two endings feel different enough?
Length: about a minute, eleven rooms. Too long, too short, or right for a fever dream?
Does each room still read as a room of this house (the kitchen, the hallway, Theo's room, the attic), or do they blur together?
The stairwell door is the hardest spot. After two falls there, the dream offers to let her through in exchange for a memory. Does that offer feel right, or should the spot just be easier?
notes: Each room has its two walls and a ceiling. In the tipped rooms that means the old floor on the left, the old ceiling on the right and the papered old wall overhead; the last hall is the right way up; the attic is in its boards. The observatory stays open to the night, with a framed doorway into the attic.

Fixed: the walls now run each room's whole length, so no sky shows under the ceilings over the slides and gaps; next to a wall she runs along, only the strip above it is added, so that wall still stands out.
Theo's answer pays off too: as Lena turns Nadia out, he has a parting line that depends on what she told him (honest, comfort or silence). The lines are placeholders.
The walls and ceilings are only pictures and have no collision, so the course, its wallruns and its timings are unchanged.
